newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk IMP aims to boost sales by 30 pct.
newsitem.headline: Turk IMP aims to boost sales by 30 pct.

text.p: Turkish engine piston and gudgeon pin producer Istanbul Motor Piston ve Pim Sanayi A.S. (IMP) aims to boost sales by around 30 percent after achieving its targets for the first half of the year, a senior company official said on Tuesday.

"This year we aim to utilise 100 percent of the capacity to produce 2.2 million units of pistons and to increase the turnover by approximately 30 percent," finance manager Erdin Ozdemir told Reuters, adding that market conditions were right for such an expansion.
The company produced 1.6 million units of engine pistons and pins with 72 percent capacity utilisation for a 1.9 trillion lira ($12 million) turnover and 507 billion lira net profit last year.
Shares in the company opened at 17,500 lira on the Istanbul Stock Exchange on Tuesday, against 17,250 at close of business on Monday.
The company's production is mostly driven by orders from the domestic and international automotive producers.
"The rest of the production is for the spare parts market and we never rely on the weak orders of this market," Ozdemir said. "We rely on our experience and senses," he added.
Car makers Toyota and Opel, already established in Turkey, will be joined by Hyundai this year and Honda next year.
But IMP completed its capacity-expanding investments three years ago and no new expansion expected in the near future, despite the presence of new car makers.
"Because it will take time to use our products for the new car makers. Even Opel and Toyota are still importing the piston segment and body combination of the engine," he said.
"But in line with their programmes to use locally produced parts, our product's turn will come and then we will take capacity expanding investment into consideration," he added.
The company spends around $1 million on modernisation, renovation and quality adjustment investments every year.
Last year the British T&N PLC and the owner family formed a 50/50 joint venture, T&N Dereli Holding, which now holds 56.6 percent of IMP.
Ozdemir said around 10 percent of total production was exported to the UK, Italy, Greece, Bulgaria, Pakistan, Nigeria, Egypt and Iran.
IMP reported 600 billion lire turnover in the first quarter of the year against 364 billion in the same period of 1996. The net profit of the company increased to 144 billion from 118 billion.
Osman Senkul -- Istanbul newsroom / 90-212-2750875 ($ = 158990 Turkish Lire)
